title: Uses of the datetime module
description:
Think, what can you use the datetime module for? Examples: Time series analysis, To get a timestamp of any activities in an application, Adding posts on a blog

Python-Gym adaptation: this is an open-ended reflection question in the original material with no single correct answer, so it can't be checked against one fixed expected value. Implement as datetime_module_use_cases(), returning a list of the example use cases given in the exercise, as strings.
examples:
>>> datetime_module_use_cases()
['Time series analysis', 'To get a timestamp of any activities in an application', 'Adding posts on a blog']
hints: This is a reflection question - there is no calculation involved, just list some real-world uses of dates and times in software.
The exercise itself names three examples: time series analysis, timestamping activities in an application, and adding posts on a blog.
Return a list literal containing at least those example use cases as strings, e.g. ['Time series analysis', ...].
expected_behavior: Returns a list of strings naming example real-world use cases for the datetime module.

hidden_tests.call: all(isinstance(x, str) for x in datetime_module_use_cases())
hidden_tests.label: every use case is a string

explanation: This exercise is a reflection prompt rather than a calculation, so the hidden tests only check the shape of the answer (a list of at least 3 strings) rather than its exact wording, since the original material itself only offers open-ended examples.
